blocks.md: Layout with one folder per song and one file per stem (MUSDB18 style). All stems must end at the same moment.

blocks.label: Glossary term · Dataset type 2
blocks.md: Dataset type 2

blocks.label: Definition · Layout with one folder per stem, containing every song of that…
blocks.md: Layout with one folder per stem, containing every song of that stem. Random chunks are mixed on the fly, so track lengths need not match.

blocks.label: Glossary term · dim_t
blocks.md: dim\_t

blocks.label: Definition · How many spectrogram frames the window divides into — the same…
blocks.md: How many spectrogram frames the window divides into — the same fact as `chunk_size` in different units. Every STFT here pads with `center=True`, so `chunk_size = (dim_t − 1) × hop_length` exactly. In a Roformer config the `audio.dim_t` line is ignored; the frame count follows from `audio.chunk_size` and `model.stft_hop_length`.

blocks.label: Glossary term · chunk_size
blocks.md: chunk\_size

blocks.label: Definition · The audio window in samples that the model is trained on — the…
blocks.md: The audio window in samples that the model is trained on — the one key *every* architecture reads from the config. Your main lever for fitting a run into limited VRAM, and the window the frame count is derived from: frames = `chunk_size ÷ hop_length + 1`.

blocks.label: Glossary term · hop_length
blocks.md: hop\_length

blocks.label: Definition · The step between spectrogram frames, in samples — a property of…
blocks.md: The step between spectrogram frames, in samples — a property of the model's STFT rather than a free preference. Every published Roformer uses a hundredth of the sample rate (`441` at 44.1 kHz, so a frame is 10 ms); the MSST templates and DTTNet use `n_fft ÷ 4` (`512` at `n_fft: 2048`), and mdx23c uses `n_fft ÷ 8`. Which key counts depends on the architecture: `model.stft_hop_length` for the Roformer family, `audio.hop_length` for mdx23c and DTTNet, `model.hop_size` for SCNet. In a Roformer config the `audio` copy is ignored. It also sets the memory: at a fixed window, half the hop is twice the frames.

blocks.label: Glossary term · n_fft
blocks.md: n\_fft

blocks.label: Definition · The STFT window length in samples — 2048 in every Roformer conf…
blocks.md: The STFT window length in samples — `2048` in every Roformer config here. It sets the frequency resolution and, indirectly, the model's size: `dim_f`, the mel bands the transformer reads, is half of it, so `n_fft: 2048` means `dim_f: 1024`. Read it from `model.stft_n_fft` in a Roformer config and from `audio.n_fft` in mdx23c or DTTNet.

blocks.label: Glossary term · sample rate
blocks.md: sample rate

blocks.label: Definition · The rate the model's spectrogram is built from, and therefore t…
blocks.md: The rate the model's spectrogram is built from, and therefore the highest frequency it can ever reproduce: half the rate, no more.

blocks.label: Glossary term · Nyquist frequency
blocks.md: Nyquist frequency

blocks.label: Definition · Half the sample rate — the ceiling on what that rate can repres…
blocks.md: Half the sample rate — the ceiling on what that rate can represent. At 44 100 Hz it is 22 050 Hz; everything above it is discarded before training begins.

blocks.label: Glossary term · Stereo / mono
blocks.md: Stereo / mono

blocks.label: Definition · An architecture setting, not a file format. audio.num_channels…
blocks.md: An architecture setting, not a file format. `audio.num_channels: 2` with `model.stereo: true` is what every published Roformer uses; a mono model is `num_channels: 1` with `stereo: false`, and its attention sequence — and so its memory — is about half.

blocks.md: One full pass through `num_steps` updates. The trainer validates and stores weights at the end of each one.

blocks.md: One weight update. Validation happens every `num_steps` steps.

blocks.md: Gradient accumulation

heading.label: Chapter heading · Appendix B · Metric reference

blocks.label: Paragraph · The numbers the trainer prints. They exist to tell you which di…
blocks.md: The numbers the trainer prints. They exist to tell you which direction a run is moving — not to declare a model finished.

blocks.label: Label · The trade-off you will meet first
blocks.md: The trade-off you will meet first

blocks.label: Paragraph · Fullness and bleedless move against each other. Push the target…
blocks.md: **Fullness and bleedless move against each other.** Push the target stem to sound fuller and more of the other stem tends to leak in; push bleed down and the target starts sounding thin. Pick the end of that scale your material needs — an instrumental for a karaoke track wants bleedless, a stem for remixing may prefer fullness.

blocks.label: Bold label · ↑ Fullness
blocks.md: ↑ Fullness

blocks.label: Label · The target sounds complete and nothing feels missing — at the c…
blocks.md: The target sounds complete and nothing feels missing — at the cost of more bleed from the other stem.

blocks.label: Bold label · ↑ Bleedless
blocks.md: ↑ Bleedless

blocks.label: Label · The leak from the other stem disappears — but the target can st…
blocks.md: The leak from the other stem disappears — but the target can start sounding thin or hollow.

blocks.label: Paragraph · A checkpoint sits somewhere on this line, not at the end of it…
blocks.md: A checkpoint sits somewhere on this line, not at the end of it. Decide which way your material leans *before* you chase a number.

blocks.label: Subheading · Choosing the scheduler metric
blocks.md: Choosing the scheduler metric

blocks.label: Paragraph · --metric_for_scheduler decides which of these numbers drives th…
blocks.md: `--metric_for_scheduler` decides which of these numbers drives the learning-rate scheduler: while the chosen metric keeps improving, the rate holds; when it stalls for `patience` epochs, the rate is multiplied by `reduce_factor`. `sdr` is the usual choice, with `fullness` or `bleedless` as alternatives when you care about one specific behaviour.

blocks.label: Label · Metrics are numbers — listen to the audio
blocks.md: Metrics are numbers — listen to the audio

blocks.label: Paragraph · Use metrics for a quick evaluation and for spotting trend chang…
blocks.md: Use metrics for a quick evaluation and for spotting trend changes. They will not tell you whether a song sounds good. Export a few tracks with the checkpoint, listen on the material you actually care about, and treat the numbers as a smoke detector rather than a verdict.
